offers.name: Acer Nitro V 15.6" 165Hz Gaming Laptop - AMD Ryzen 5 7535HS - 8GB DDR5 - 512GB SSD - RTX 3050 - Windows 11 - Black

reviews.quote: For the price, we have to applaud the Nitro V 15 on most fronts; it delivers steady 1080p gaming performance at a much lower price than most competitors.
Notebookcheck's Nitro V 15 (ANV15) review collection averages 72.17% across 66 reviews - a good budget gaming showing.
An ultra-affordable gaming laptop that gets the basics right for 1080p play.

praises: At $1,099.95 sale it is the cheapest way into a real RTX GPU with a 165Hz IPS panel in Canada
USB4 40Gbps port with power delivery and HDMI 2.1 + RJ-45 Ethernet — port set of a $1,800 machine
Ryzen 5 7535HS is a proper 6C/12T gaming CPU and stays cool thanks to the dual-fan Nitro cooling
165Hz IPS panel is smooth and bright enough for its class
Backlit keyboard and 2x SO-DIMM + M.2 slots make it genuinely serviceable
complaints: 8GB single-stick DDR5 cripples the RTX 3050 — single-channel memory costs 15-20% FPS out of the box
RTX 3050's 4GB VRAM chokes on 2025/2026 AAA titles at high settings; medium settings are the reality
Battery life is short (~3-4h) — normal for entry gaming but a shock coming from a thin-and-light
Plasticky chassis with a noticeable wobble; build is a step below LOQ/Legion
720p webcam and average speakers; fan curve is aggressive once gaming

standouts: Cheapest dedicated-GPU gaming entry in the dataset at sale ($1,099.95) with an unusually rich port set (USB4, HDMI 2.1, RJ-45)
dealbreakers: 8GB single-channel RAM out of the box — budget the $25 second stick immediately or the RTX 3050 underperforms badly
design_philosophy: Acer's door into gaming: last-generation AMD CPU plus the oldest GPU still worth selling (RTX 3050), wrapped in the genuinely good Nitro V cooling and an over-spec port list (USB4, HDMI 2.1, Ethernet) that punches above the price. The single cost cut that actually matters is 8GB single-channel RAM — an intentional, fixable tax. Category-listed as budget because its sale price lands in the budget cart, but it is entry gaming, not an office laptop.
